correctness.rationale: For g=t^(1/n) product L_j(t)^(-beta_j), q=t g′/g tends to 1/n and tg″/g tends to 1/n^2-1/n<0, so chi(s)=-g(-s) is eventually increasing and convex. Chen–Shao–Wang Theorem 1.5 reduces the entire Monge–Ampère question to ∫g^(n-2)g′²dt = ∫q²/[t product L_j^(n beta_j)]dt. The ordinary generalized-log integral converges iff the first exponent differing from 1 is greater than 1. Thm 1.2 gives W1,2 because 2/n-2<-1 for n>=3, Thm1.3(ii) excludes W2,1 since g tends to infinity, and Thm1.1 provides an L1 Laplacian since g′→0 and ∫|g″| is finite.
